clue.text: Magnate bringing second shift back

parts.note: MO is short for a moment, a second

indicators.note: back says the word for shift is read in reverse order

parts.note: to lug something is to shift it with effort

explanation.surface: A tycoon arranges for the second shift to return to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work rota; it is the verb, to haul, and 'back' turns that word around.
explanation.definitionFit: A mogul is a powerful business figure, the same sense as a tycoon.

clue.text: The old are past it

parts.note: read as a riddle: the elderly have already gone through the stage of life between youth and old age

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that elderly people are no longer up to things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past it' seems to mean too old to cope; read literally, the old have passed beyond a certain stage of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle age is the life stage elderly people have already lived through.

clue.text: Praise good and colourful speaker

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot, a bird that can talk

explanation.surface: Commending a fine, vivid orator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colourful speaker' sounds like a lively orator, but it is a talking bird, the bright parrot called a lory.
explanation.definitionFit: To give glory to someone is to give them praise or honour.

clue.text: Recording problem with ship

definitions.meaning: ... things means entering them in a record or register
a ship that leans to one side is said to be doing this

explanation.surface: A fault noted in the log of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Listing means both writing items down in a list and a ship's tilting over to one side.

clue.text: In peevish irritation, favoured university cut

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
to lance is to cut open with a blade

explanation.surface: A favourite college's funding is slashed, causing grumpy resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky bad temper, the same as peevishness.

clue.text: Tiny amount charged for fashion

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
ton is an old word for high fashion

explanation.surface: Only a small fee is billed for a fashion item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' looks like billing, but it means electrically charged; TON as fashion is an old usage, as in 'bon ton'.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton is a minute subatomic particle carrying a positive electric charge.

clue.text: Timber, as it is treated inside to make paper

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged letters go within the word for timber

parts.note: a tree is a source of timber, and in older usage timber itself

indicators.note: something treated is processed or worked on, so the letters of as it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wood, once processed, is turned into paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is treated' signals the rearrangement of 'as it', and 'inside' sets the result within the timber word.
explanation.definitionFit: A treatise is a formal written study, the kind of thing called an academic paper.

clue.text: Throwing some light on tendency to strike

indicators.note: to says the word for tendency is attached to the word for strike

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike
a bent is an inclination or tendency

explanation.surface: Explaining someone's urge to hit out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing some light on' reads as explaining; the definition means glowing softly, with 'on' a link. 'to' attaches the tendency word after the strike word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent describes a soft, flickering glow, so it means giving off a little light.

clue.text: Bat Henry's left in the attic jumble

indicators.note: left means gone away, so the letter for Henry departs from the mix
a jumble is a disordered mixture, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A bat has escaped into the clutter of an attic after Henry has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' looks like the animal in an attic, but it is the verb, as in batting an eyelid. Take H from IN THE ATTIC and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To nictitate is to blink, and to bat the eyelids is to blink them.

clue.text: Acceptable, during a previous night, to call out

indicators.note: during says one word sits within the span of the other

parts.note: an eve is the evening or day before an event
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: It is fine to shout out on the evening before.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon or call forth, as in calling up a memory.

clue.text: Decline, at historic Scottish site, the local pancake

parts.note: a drop is a fall or decline
Scone, near Perth, is where Scottish kings were crowned on the Stone of Scone

explanation.surface: A fall in standards at an ancient Scottish place, compared with the regional griddle cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the local' ties the pancake to Scotland, where the drop scone is a traditional griddle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop scone is a small thick pancake cooked on a griddle, a Scottish speciality.

clue.text: Run from the demo and duck aggressive male

indicators.note: from says the letter for run is taken out of the word for demo

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Flee the protest and dodge a thuggish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run from' sounds like fleeing; it tells you to take the run letter out of the protest word, and a duck is a cricket score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho describes a man who is aggressively and showily masculine.

clue.text: What train-wrecker does with boulder? Takes risk with it

definitions.meaning: literally, a saboteur places a big rock across the railway track
the idiom means staking something, such as a job or reputation, on an outcome

explanation.surface: A saboteur blocks the railway with a rock, gambling on the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means putting something at risk, and literally describes placing an object across rails.

clue.text: Part of Ireland Graham converted

indicators.note: something converted is changed in form, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Graham has found religion somewhere in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suggests religious conversion, but it rearranges GRAHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagh is a county and city in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: High Italian mass affected by upheaval?

definitions.text: High Italian mass affected by upheaval?

parts.words: High Italian mass affected by upheaval?
parts.note: read as a religious service in Italy disrupted, but meaning a tall Sicilian peak that erupts

explanation.surface: A grand Catholic service in Italy thrown into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' and 'mass' suggest a church service; the mass is a mountain in Sicily, and upheaval is volcanic eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is the tall active volcano in Sicily, a high mass of rock repeatedly upheaved by eruptions.

clue.text: They contain the remains, when coffin nails are finished

definitions.text: They contain the remains, when coffin nails are finished

parts.words: They contain the remains, when coffin nails are finished
parts.note: reads like funeral urns, but coffin nails is slang for cigarettes and the remains are their stubs

explanation.surface: Urns hold human ashes once the coffin has been sealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coffin nails' is old slang for cigarettes, so the remains are ash and stubs, not a body.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashtrays are receptacles for cigarette ash and butts once smoked.

clue.text: Lead for tip of weapon

definitions.meaning: to lead an attack or campaign from the front
the pointed head fixed to a throwing or thrusting shaft

explanation.surface: Bullet metal used to make the point of a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal; it is the verb, to be at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead is to lead a campaign, and literally it is the point of a spear.

clue.text: Gushing and unrestrained piece of writing

definitions.meaning: a pouring out of liquid, used here as a noun
an over-emotional, flowing outpouring of words

explanation.surface: A rush of emotional, uncontrolled prose.
explanation.definitionFit: An effusion is a pouring forth of liquid and also an extravagant outpouring of words.

clue.text: Use filmy mixture to make a colloid

indicators.note: a mixture is a jumbled combination, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Apply a thin-layered blend to produce a colloidal substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture' looks chemical, fitting the surface, but it rearranges USE FILMY.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulsify is to disperse one liquid in another, forming a colloid called an emulsion.

clue.text: Composer who makes a mark?

definitions.meaning: Sir John ... was a Victorian English composer of church music
one who stains, leaving a mark

explanation.surface: Asking which composer left a lasting impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainer was an English composer, and a stainer is literally someone or something that leaves a stain.

clue.text: In terms of this unit, I may measure up

definitions.text: In terms of this unit, I may measure up

parts.words: In terms of this unit, I may measure up
parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current, and current is measured in a particular unit

explanation.surface: Someone hoping to prove good enough by a certain standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' reads as the speaker, but in physics I stands for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current, the quantity written as I.

clue.text: Weapon guerrilla leader used in China

indicators.note: used in says the guerrilla's name is put inside the other word

parts.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate
Che Guevara led guerrilla forces in the Cuban revolution

explanation.surface: A guerrilla chief's weapon deployed in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; it is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade, which can serve as a weapon.

clue.text: Coastal defence taking George I a year to install

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: to install means fitting the letter for year inside the word for I

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sea barrier that took King George I a whole year to put in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George I' reads as the king; it splits into the royal cipher for George and the number one, with the year letter set inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A groyne is a low wall built out into the sea to check erosion of a beach.

clue.text: Off course?

parts.note: reads as having strayed from a route, but means outside the curriculum of study

explanation.surface: A navigator wondering if the ship has strayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a route; here it is a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: Extracurricular activities lie outside the regular course of study.

clue.text: Volatile liquid repeatedly necessary to fire the rocket here

indicators.note: what is necessary to a phrase is contained in it, so the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A volatile fuel needed again and again for launching a rocket.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'rocket here'; 'repeatedly' and 'fire the' only dress the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a highly volatile, flammable solvent once used as an anaesthetic.

clue.text: Drink up about four pints?

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning
GAL is short for gallon, a liquid measure; a gallon is in fact eight pints, so the setter's figure is loose

explanation.surface: Knocking back a good four pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RE + GAL; the question mark covers the setter's loose arithmetic, since a gallon is eight pints.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light beer, a common drink.

clue.text: Discover it in the return of classical drama

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Discover it in the return of classical drama' (3,2): reversed NOH gives HON, but nothing gives AT, and 'Discover' means the opposite of HAT ON; the clue looks misread (perhaps 'Don't discover' or similar)
annotationWithheld.clue: Discover it in the return of classical drama

clue.text: Climber has a long way to go in top college group

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A mountaineer faces a long trek to reach an elite university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of eight prestigious universities in the north-eastern United States.

clue.text: Make adjustment on Scottish island with good English

parts.note: re means on, concerning
Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

explanation.surface: Making changes on a Scottish island with a decent Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearrange is to alter the order of things, which is making an adjustment.

clue.text: Prepared to listen, like either half of Cornwall?

definitions.meaning: having ears, so equipped for hearing
corn grows ears and walls are said to have ears, so both halves of the county name have them

explanation.surface: A Cornish listener ready to hear the gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall, the county in south-west England, splits into CORN (which grows in ears) and WALL (walls have ears, as the saying goes).
explanation.definitionFit: Eared means having ears, so equipped to hear; corn is eared and walls proverbially have ears.
